applicable_when: The kernel launches 124,416 CTAs across 132 SMs (58.91 waves). Each CTA processes a small [BLOCK_OH, BLOCK_OW] output tile and terminates. With 58+ waves, the GPU repeatedly re-schedules CTAs, incurring launch/scheduling overhead per wave. The kernel is ALU-bound (84% compute SOL, 80.3% ALU pipeline) with 35.5B instructions. A persistent kernel replaces the 3D grid with a 1D grid of exactly num_SMs*4 CTAs; each CTA loops over a flat tile index using tl.atomic_add on a shared counter. This eliminates wave-boundary idle time, reduces scheduler pressure from CTA launch, and allows the compiler to keep more loop-invariant values in registers across tile iterations. All prior optimization attempts (hoisting, coalescing, transposing) failed with a Triton pointer-argument error, so this is a structurally different approach that avoids those pitfalls.

In Triton, a 2D block [M, N] is laid out in row-major order: consecutive thread IDs (within a warp) vary along the LAST dimension (N = BLOCK_OW). The inp_ptrs computation is `input_ptr + inp_base + ih_ptrs[:, None] + iw_ptrs[None, :]`, producing a [BLOCK_OH, BLOCK_OW] pointer array. Consecutive threads in a warp cover the BLOCK_OW (inner) dimension, mapping to IW (stride s_iiw=1 contiguous). However, NCU reports only 20.1/32 bytes utilized per sector, indicating strided access. The root cause: with BLOCK_OH as the outer dimension, each warp covers BLOCK_OW consecutive IW addresses per row, but across different OH rows — the ih_ptrs[:, None] term introduces a stride of s_iih=IW=64 elements between rows, causing multiple cache-line fetches per warp when BLOCK_OH > 1. Fix: swap accumulator shape to [BLOCK_OW, BLOCK_OH] so OW (fast/contiguous) is the OUTER dimension iterated by consecutive thread IDs. Previous attempt (item 172acfc2) failed with 'ValueError: Pointer argument' — a Triton launch config error, NOT a logic error. The transposition approach is correct; the fix must preserve pointer types and grid lambda.
